findings: The five-minute grace runs recovered task execution in 66.5 and 94.0 seconds.
The three-second grace run recovered task execution in 94.3 seconds. Shortening that setting did not remove the delay.
During shutdown, the queue thread waited in GracefulEmbeddedServiceShutdownListener.onApplicationEvent through CompletableFuture.join.
Shutdown callbacks waited in JdbcQueue.poll through Awaitility and in JdbcQueue.close through ThreadPoolExecutor.awaitTermination.
HTTP 200 responses continued before task execution recovered.
The dynamic port changed after Docker restarted Kestra. The corrected probe follows the current binding.
Applying the profile limits of two CPUs and 2 GiB produced 67.1-second task recovery. Those limits alone did not reproduce the longer distributed shutdown.
limits: These focused runs do not override the retained distributed PostgreSQL recovery failure.
